# VescIf — VescInterface

The connection, configuration and file-transfer facade. A package reaches it as the `VescIf` context property on desktop and as the `VescIf` singleton on mobile; both resolve the same object, so write `VescIf.` and nothing else.

`commands()`, `mcConfig()`, `appConfig()`, `customConfig(i)` return live child objects. Read them once into a property (`property Commands mCommands: VescIf.commands()`) instead of calling them inside bindings.

Signatures use C++ types. In QML: `QString` is a JS string, `QVector<T>` and `QStringList` are JS arrays, `QVariantMap` is a plain JS object, `QVariantList` an array, `QByteArray` an `ArrayBuffer` (read with a `DataView`), and `QVariant` anything.

Generated from vesc_tool `a34c1727` (working tree dirty).
